problem:
Let $V=C[0,\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,\pi ]\,,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

If $x(t)=1$ and $y(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-k$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
worked_solution:
Since $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-k)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)-kt){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\pi k-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =-\pi k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\pi k & =0 \\ k & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
